entities.name: Achille Le Tonnelier de Breteuil
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Achille Le Tonnelier de Breteuil (1781–1864) emerged as a key administrative and political figure during France's tumultuous post-Napoleonic era, serving the Bourbon Restoration and the July Monarchy. Born into an ancient noble family with deep roots in the French aristocracy, he navigated the shifting political landscape from prefectural administration to the legislative chambers of the Peerage. His career exemplifies the efforts of a segment of the old nobility to adapt and contribute to the re-establishment of monarchical order after decades of revolution and empire, embodying a blend of conservative loyalty and administrative pragmatism.

His public service began in earnest during the First Restoration, where he was appointed Prefect of the Eure department in 1814, a crucial role in consolidating royal authority in the provinces. Following the Hundred Days, he was reinstated and continued to serve as Prefect of Eure until 1820. His administrative acumen earned him a promotion to the Chamber of Peers in 1827, where he sat among the ultra-royalist faction, advocating for policies that aimed to restore traditional values and institutions. During the July Monarchy, he continued his senatorial duties, albeit with a more cautious approach, and briefly served as ambassador to Modena, further extending his influence into diplomatic circles.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Achille de Breteuil's career as a prefect and Peer of France significantly contributed to the administrative and legislative stability of post-Napoleonic France, representing the efforts of the old nobility to adapt to new political realities. His consistent service helped shape the governance of two successive monarchies.
